name: Clean Energy Fuels Corp.

profile.description: Clean Energy Fuels Corp. is the largest provider of renewable natural gas (RNG) fuel for the transportation market in North America, operating 600+ fueling stations and supplying RNG, CNG, and LNG for medium and heavy-duty vehicle fleets. The company invests in upstream dairy farm RNG production through partnerships with TotalEnergies and BP, and is expanding into power generation and hydrogen fuel. Co-founded by T. Boone Pickens in 1997, the company transitioned from long-time CEO Andrew Littlefair to Clay Corbus in 2026. Q2 2026 revenue of $106.4M with 63.2M RNG gallons sold (+2.9% YoY), and Q1 2026 beat estimates at $117.6M (+13.3%). Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $456M. Market cap ~$368M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Clean Energy executed a meaningful vertical integration over the last five years, transitioning from pure fuel distribution to upstream RNG production through dairy farm partnerships with TotalEnergies and BP, opening new revenue streams from environmental credit sales [1]. Q2 2026 highlights show the company expanding into power generation and hydrogen fuel, representing further diversification beyond core RNG distribution [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products, AI-driven cost savings, or AI deployment initiatives evident in earnings calls or filings. The company uses AI monitoring in fleet vehicles operationally but has not commercialized any AI capabilities [2]. Market Share (2/2): Clean Energy is the nation's largest RNG provider for transportation with 600+ fueling stations across North America — dominant category leadership with specific infrastructure that no competitor matches in scale [1][3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised from $410M to $456M, RNG production ramp-up continues with dairy farm projects under development, and expansion into power generation and hydrogen fuel create new growth vectors [1]. However, specific facility launch dates and capacity targets remain vague. R&D Intensity (0/1): Minimal R&D spending as a percentage of revenue; capital investment is directed toward physical infrastructure buildout (fueling stations, dairy digesters) rather than traditional R&D [4].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Clean Energy's mission to decarbonize transportation through renewable natural gas is specific and thoughtful — it identifies a particular mechanism (converting organic waste to fuel), a specific sector (heavy-duty transportation), and a tangible environmental outcome [3]. The mission was forged by co-founder T. Boone Pickens' vision for American energy independence in 1997 and has been maintained through his death in 2019 and CEO transitions. The Inspire Impact Score of 72 (ALIGNED) with zero negative attributions reflects this genuine environmental purpose. Community Impact (1/2): Dairy RNG projects convert agricultural methane waste into vehicle fuel, providing measurable environmental benefits to farming communities. The fueling network directly serves public transit, refuse trucks, and municipal fleets, reducing community-level emissions from essential services [1][3]. Employee Retention (0/2): No specific voluntary turnover rates, average tenure data, or evidence that employees cite the mission as a retention driver was identified for the 503-employee workforce. Employee feedback is mixed regarding culture and leadership [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by executives in the last 12 months. New CEO Clay Corbus has 20 years at the company and significant equity exposure through tenure, but no recent open-market purchases were identified.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics excluding PEG (unavailable due to negative earnings). D/E of 57.74% is well within the 70% target (score 1.0) [4]. However, ROE of -16.4% and profit margin of -21.27% reflect ongoing unprofitability, scoring 0.0 on both metrics at 2x and 1x weight respectively. Forward P/E of -41.75 indicates expected losses continuing, scoring 0.0. Revenue growth is modest: TTM YoY of 3.7% (score 0.79) and 5-year CAGR of ~7.8% (score 0.85 at 2x weight) both below the 10% targets [1]. Q1 2026 showed improvement with net loss narrowing from $(135)M to $(12.4)M YoY, and Q2 2026 loss of $(14.9)M was also improved from $(20.2)M prior year [1]. Weighted sum 3.50/8 = 4.37, rounds to 4. Liquidity floor passes: 1.95M avg volume x $1.67 = $3.25M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Clean Energy's core business is fundamentally physical — operating 600+ fueling stations, producing RNG from dairy farms and landfills, and managing fuel logistics and distribution infrastructure across North America [3]. AI cannot substitute for physical fuel production, pipeline infrastructure, or station operations. The competitive moat rests on the fueling network, long-term fleet contracts, and RNG production partnerships with TotalEnergies and BP — all physical-world assets immune to AI disruption [1]. The primary disruption risk comes from EV adoption displacing natural gas vehicles, but that is a technology transition risk not an AI substitution risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue streams identified. The company deploys AI monitoring in work vehicles for operational purposes but has not commercialized any AI capabilities or reported AI-driven efficiency gains [2].

infinite_game.summary: Clean Energy plays a mostly infinite game — maintaining its core purpose of decarbonizing heavy-duty transportation through renewable natural gas for 29 years, surviving the death of co-founder T. Boone Pickens and multiple CEO transitions. The vertical integration into RNG production and expansion into hydrogen and power generation show willingness to evolve. However, the cause is tied to a specific technology (RNG) rather than a transcendent vision, and mixed employee sentiment suggests the infinite mindset has not fully permeated the organization.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Clean Energy has a genuine and distinctive purpose — decarbonizing heavy-duty transportation through renewable natural gas derived from organic waste. This cause connects the company's work to climate change mitigation and has been consistently pursued since 1997 [3]. The cause survived co-founder T. Boone Pickens' death in 2019 and two CEO transitions, with successor Clay Corbus (20 years at the company) continuing the same strategic direction [2]. The Inspire Impact Score of 72 (ALIGNED) validates genuine environmental commitment. However, the cause is tied to a specific technology rather than a transcendent vision — if RNG becomes obsolete, the cause may not survive the transition.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Clean Energy has continued investing in capital-intensive dairy RNG production projects and expanded into power generation and hydrogen fuel despite years of GAAP losses, betting that long-term renewable fuel transition will justify current capital deployment [1]. The decision to invest in upstream production while operating at a loss — with net losses narrowing from $(135)M to $(12.4)M in Q1 2026 — shows willingness to sacrifice near-term profitability for long-term capability. However, these investments are supported by regulatory tailwinds (LCFS credits, RFS) rather than contrarian bets against market consensus.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong — the CEO transition from Littlefair to Corbus maintained strategic direction, and Corbus' 20-year tenure signals deep organizational commitment [2]. The company's small size (503 employees) creates proximity between leadership and teams. However, employee feedback cites culture and senior leadership as concerns, with criticism of poor management and limited advancement opportunities [2]. No specific retention or tenure data was available to confirm above-average trust.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Clean Energy evolved from a pure CNG/LNG fuel distributor to a vertically integrated RNG producer through dairy farm partnerships, and is now expanding into power generation and hydrogen fuel — meaningful strategic evolution [1]. Q2 2026 earnings highlighted RNG production ramp-up and hydrogen fuel growth as new business vectors. However, the core business model of fueling vehicles at physical stations has remained fundamentally unchanged for decades, and the company has not demonstrated willingness to abandon its fueling infrastructure model if electrification demands it.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of an infinite competitive mindset in management commentary. Clean Energy positions itself as 'the largest provider of the cleanest fuel' — language emphasizing dominance and superiority rather than learning from competitors [3]. No acknowledgment of EV competitors' strengths or discussion of how competitive pressure from Tesla Semi, Daimler eActros, or hydrogen alternatives improves Clean Energy's own offerings.

investment_thesis: Clean Energy Fuels is the dominant RNG provider for North American heavy-duty transportation with 600+ fueling stations and growing production capacity through dairy farm partnerships with TotalEnergies and BP [3]. Q1 2026 beat estimates at $117.6M revenue (+13.3% YoY) with EPS of $(0.06) vs. prior year $(0.60), and Q2 2026 delivered $106.4M with continued loss narrowing to $(0.07) per share from $(0.09) [1]. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $456M represents meaningful growth acceleration, and the expansion into power generation and hydrogen fuel diversifies revenue beyond core fueling. The Inspire Impact Score of 72 (ALIGNED) with zero negative attributions makes this an exceptionally clean faith-based investment in the energy transition. At $1.67 per share and $368M market cap, the stock offers significant upside if the company achieves profitability on its growing revenue base.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on persistent unprofitability, existential technology risk, and the stock's penny-stock valuation. At -21.27% profit margin and -16.4% ROE, Clean Energy has never achieved sustained GAAP profitability despite $430M+ in annual revenue and 29 years of operations [4]. The stock has declined from $1.86 to $1.67 since the prior screen, trading below its 50-day moving average of $1.80, reflecting continued market skepticism. The rapid adoption of battery-electric trucks by major fleet operators (Amazon, FedEx, UPS) threatens to strand CLNE's fueling infrastructure as a transitional technology, and the company's sub-$400M market cap creates meaningful equity dilution risk if capital raises are needed. Revenue growth decelerated from 13.3% in Q1 to 3.7% in Q2 2026, and heavy dependence on government credits (LCFS, RINs) exposes revenue to regulatory policy risk under changing administrations [1]. The Altman Z-Score signals elevated financial distress risk for a company still burning cash.
key_catalysts: Accelerating path toward profitability with net losses narrowing dramatically — from $(135)M to $(12.4)M in Q1 and $(20.2)M to $(14.9)M in Q2 YoY — and full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $456M [1]
Expansion into power generation and hydrogen fuel creates new revenue vectors beyond core RNG fueling, with Q2 2026 earnings highlighting both as growth drivers [1]

Upstream RNG production capacity ramp-up through dairy farm partnerships shifting revenue mix toward higher-margin owned production, with 63.2M RNG gallons sold in Q2 representing continued volume growth [1]
key_risks: Persistent GAAP unprofitability after 29 years of operations with -21.27% profit margin and -16.4% ROE — the company has never demonstrated ability to sustainably earn positive returns on equity [4]

Battery-electric truck adoption by major fleet operators could strand the 600+ fueling station network as a transitional technology, particularly as BEV total cost of ownership improves for long-haul routes

Heavy reliance on regulatory credits (LCFS, RINs) exposes revenue to policy risk — any reduction in credit values or program scope could materially impact economics, and the $368M market cap creates dilution risk if capital raises are needed [1]
